newsitem.title: UK: Hyder lobbies government over windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: Hyder lobbies government over windfall tax.

text.p: British multi-utility Hyder Plc confirmed on Thursday it was lobbying the government over its share of a one-off tax on excess profits of privatised utilities, because it feels it has been penalised over other companies.

A report in the Evening Standard newspaper said chief executive Graham Hawker felt the company had been unfairly penalised because the tax is based on pre-exceptional profits and because its water group, Welsh Water, cut costs quickly after privatisation.

"It is bizarre that we have been so badly penalised, particularly as we are acknowledged to be a customer-oriented company. We are asking the government to do something to ameliorate the extreme hit on Hyder," the newspaper quoted Hawker saying.
Hyder's share of the total 5.2 billion stg tax, announced in the new Labour government's first budget on July 2, is 282 million stg, above most expectations of around 230 million.

The tax will be charged at a rate of 23 percent on the difference between company value at the time of flotation and company value calculated by reference to net profits over a period of up to four years following privatisation.
The company has ruled out a legal challenge to the tax and said it would pay its share from borrowings.

The government made the so-called "windfall" tax on the utilities, privatised by previous Conservative administations, a central plank of its manifesto which helped bring it to power in a landslide victory on May 1. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
